card.name: Switching to an alternative treatment
card.fires_on: The word "alternative" (and sometimes "be" or part of "discontinue") in instructions to stop a drug and use another therapy, such as "administer an alternative anticoagulant".

modes.label: Alternative therapy
modes.description: The word "alternative" after "an" or "institute" when telling the reader to use a different drug after stopping one.
modes.example: evaluate for HIT and HITT, and, if necessary, administer an<< alternative>> anticoagulant [see Warnings

modes.label: Other agents should be chosen
modes.description: The word "be" in a phrase saying another agent should be selected instead.
modes.example: other therapeutic agents with broader tissue distribution should<< be>> selected.

modes.label: Inside stop-drug wording
modes.description: Partway through words like discontinued or a brand name in warnings about stopping a drug.
modes.example: IF AN ALLERGIC REACTION OCCURS, BICILLIN C-R SHOULD BE DISCONT<<IN>>UED AND APPROPRIATE THER

card.writes: Little clear effect; the promoted words about assigned or preferred options loosely fit choosing a substitute.
card.plain: It lights up where a label says to stop a drug and use a different treatment instead.
